A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EMLoC and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original VQA and mathematical-reasoning experiments, resource measurements, ablations, and diffusion-model personalization results, including appendix Table 12.

after.justification: v2 reports the retained original experiments plus additional compression ablations, pipeline timing, stronger small-model comparisons, and Houlsby-adapter results.

M1.justification: The original emulator construction, LoRA training, and correction algorithm remain unchanged. Section 11.5 adds a concrete variant using Houlsby adapters instead of LoRA and applying only the first two stages, without LoRA-specific correction.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven VQA datasets, MathQA, GSM8K, LAION-COCO construction data, and DreamBooth personalization subjects. Diffusion personalization moves from v1's appendix into v2's main text; the new comparisons retain existing tasks and domains.

E2.justification: v2 adds InternVL3-2B as a stronger compact-model comparator in Table 14 and a Houlsby-adapter variant in Table 15. New Table 12 compares full-pipeline timing against LoRA and QLoRA. The original benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Added evaluations include correction ablations at 50% compression, full-pipeline timing for 8B and 38B models with specified GPU counts, and explicitly labeled WebSRC validation-set comparisons in Tables 14–15. Existing main-experiment training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 extends the component ablation to 50% compression and adds targeted checks of total runtime overhead, competitiveness against a stronger small model, and compatibility with Houlsby adapters. Existing transfer analyses, calibration-size sensitivity, and lambda sensitivity are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The estimated 38B LoRA runtime in v2 does not introduce a statistical uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Matched benchmark, resource, and diffusion results are unchanged. Added results include 8B pipeline times of 5.0 hours for EMLoC versus 11.6 for LoRA, additional ablation rows, and small-model/adapter comparisons. WebSRC scores in Tables 14–15 use validation data and should not be treated as same-setting improvements. New Table 6 reports 84.9 at 50% compression, inconsistent with the retained 85.2 in Tables 1 and 5.

T1.justification: The method equations and both supplementary derivations are retained. v1 Sections 8.1–8.2 become v2 Sections 9.1–9.2 without substantive changes to assumptions, reasoning, or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims remain memory-efficient emulator training, correction of transfer misalignment, and nonquantized 38B fine-tuning within 24GB. The abstract newly mentions the 95GB conventional requirement, but that comparison already appears in v1's main text.

C2.justification: v2 adds an interpretation linking stronger correction benefits to milder compression and better emulator alignment, and discusses full-pipeline runtime advantages. Section 11.5 explicitly limits the correction algorithm to LoRA's linear structure and states that extension to other PEFT methods is not straightforward. The original limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 discloses stage-specific elapsed times and GPU counts in Table 12, explicitly states use of gradient checkpointing alongside EMLoC, and clarifies that correction applies independently to each LoRA module. Existing hyperparameter tables and project-page access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New appendix Section 8 discusses module arithmetic through LCM-LoRA and ZipLoRA, and distinguishes EMLoC from LoRand and Houlsby adapters. These four added references refine positioning around module merging and adapter compression while retaining the original related-work framework.

P1.justification: v2 adds explanatory paragraphs and appendix subsections, moves diffusion personalization into Section 4.3, and adds acknowledgments and affiliation/publication-text updates. Most original prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 12, 14, and 15 and expands the ablation table with a compression-ratio column and two rows. The diffusion table moves into the main text, and the ablation and emulator-transfer tables exchange numbering. Figures retain their substantive content, with limited resizing and layout reflow.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's construction costs and throughput measurements, v2 provides fuller pipeline timing and additional checks of correction behavior, stronger compact models, and adapter compatibility. These additions strengthen practical validation and clarify applicability limits. The gains remain modest: the 38B timing comparison uses different GPU counts and an estimated LoRA baseline, and the new ablation introduces an unexplained 84.9 versus 85.2 WebSRC discrepancy.
